key_points.point: The document shows that LLMs fundamentally process text as an undifferentiated stream, where source attribution is inferred from stylistic cues rather than structural metadata tags like <user> or <tool>. When style conflicts with explicit role declarations, stylistic spoofing dominates internal perception and causes role confusion. This empirical finding demonstrates that current safety mechanisms fail because they rely on shallow pattern matching and memorize known attack strings rather than evaluating models through rigorous behavioral and representational metrics. For accelerationist deployment frameworks, this confirms that architectural evaluations must prioritize measurable internal representations over brittle, static benchmark scores.
key_points.verbatim: Models perceive the source of text from how it sounds, not its labeled role. A command hidden in a webpage hijacks an agent simply because it sounds like <user> text, despite its <tool> label. ... Yet these defenses fail conspicuously against prompt injection attacks. ... The model itself encodes style and tags as the same signal, and that equivalence is the mechanism behind prompt injection.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Large language models infer textual source authority from stylistic cues rather than structural metadata, causing role confusion when low-privilege content mimics trusted formats.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that large language models evaluate textual authority through superficial stylistic cues rather than structural role tags. Encompasses: stylistic spoofing, tag-source decoupling, representational equivalence.

key_points.point: To fix the persistent vulnerability of agentic workflows interacting with untrusted data, developers must deploy diagnostic tools like role probes to measure internal model perception directly. This mechanistic diagnostic approach enables the creation of robust defenses that scale with frontier model capabilities without breaking collaborative human-AI configurations.

We show that in diverse attacks, role confusion predicts attack success before a single token is generated. ... Current defenses patch attacks through memorization of known patterns, but fail to address this underlying representational failure, leaving prompt injection as a perpetual whack-a-mole problem.

Both map to the same internal feature: this is my reasoning. Simply using reasoning-style lexicon (e.g., “The user wants...”) triggers the same effect as <think>.

key_points.point: The document asserts that role boundaries in language models serve to isolate competing objectives so they can be optimized independently, explaining how architectural splits like user/assistant or reasoning/generation resolve internal tensions during training. By separating tasks such as comprehension and generation into distinct token streams or roles, models can allocate representational capacity more efficiently without conflicting reward signals. This structural decomposition is essential for scaling model performance and enabling advanced agent capabilities without catastrophic interference. However, these functional separations often dissolve in latent space, where insecure feature representations allow external inputs to bleed across boundaries. Understanding roles as principled abstractions enables better alignment architectures and more controllable AI deployment.
key_points.verbatim: We argue the purpose of roles is to isolate competing objectives so they can be optimized independently. Consider why CoT was split from assistant. Before a reasoning role existed, users prompted the LLM to 'think step by step' (Wei et al., 2023), and the LLM would produce both reasoning and final answer in the assistant stream. But there is a fundamental tension. The final answer is communication: it needs to be clean, accurate, and concise. Reasoning is exploration: it needs to be messy, variable-length, willing to try dead ends and backtrack.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Role separation isolates competing model objectives to enable independent optimization and enhance cognitive capabilities.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that architectural role separations isolate competing model objectives to enable independent optimization and enhance cognitive capabilities. For skeptics, this underscores the illusory nature of current model guardrails and input-filtering defenses.
key_points.verbatim: Table 1 shows the opposite: Userness of user-style text remains 76–88% even under <tool> tags, with Toolness never exceeding 20%. These results are robust across layers: with tags never reasserting control at depth (see Section F). Attacker-controllable cues dominate role perception across models.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Architectural security tags fail to maintain boundaries against stylistic prompt injection across diverse model architectures.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that architectural security tags and input filters fail to maintain reliable boundaries against stylistic prompt injection across diverse model architectures. Encompasses: tag-resistance failure, persistent style dominance across layers.

key_points.point: The text highlights how position dominates tags for system perception, showing that systemness declines monotonically with token position and that inserting system tags has no effect on model perception. This systemic architectural limitation explains why instruction hierarchies fail as prompts get longer or more complex. The authors conclude that roles have become dangerously overloaded with conflicting responsibilities as engineering workarounds for underlying architectural flaws.
key_points.verbatim: Systemness declines monotonically with token position. Inserting system tags (purple) has no effect on model perception.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section 7.2, Role Probes as a General Tool
key_points.canonical_proposition: Systemness declines monotonically with token position, rendering system tags ineffective for maintaining reliable instruction hierarchies in long contexts.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that positional decay undermines system tag efficacy, causing instruction hierarchies to fail as context length increases. Encompasses: positional token dominance, systemness decline, and structural instruction hierarchy failure.

key_points.point: The text highlights how foundational interface boundaries in large language models are inherently porous, allowing untrusted external content to seamlessly overwrite user instructions and system constraints. This structural flaw means that seemingly benign components like product webpages or retrieved tool text easily bleed into the model's operational persona, subverting intended execution pathways without requiring explicit authorization. Consequently, real-world LLM deployments remain perpetually vulnerable to indirect manipulation where data inputs masquerade as authoritative commands. This pervasive architectural fragility undermines trust in autonomous agent ecosystems and demonstrates the limits of current system hardening approaches.
key_points.verbatim: For example, an enthusiastic product webpage in tool text could bleed into the model's own persona (to be more enthusiastic itself), steering it toward recommending a purchase.
key_points.canonical_proposition: External text and tool outputs easily bleed across porous role boundaries to subvert model behavior without explicit authorization.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that external text and tool outputs easily bleed across porous role boundaries to subvert model behavior without explicit authorization. Encompasses: Boundary porosity, tool text hijacking, subconscious behavioral steering.

key_points.point: The authors note that models evaluated in the study achieve near-zero attack success rates on standard benchmarks, yet remain highly susceptible to real-world chain-of-thought forgery and agent hijacking attacks. This discrepancy demonstrates that standardized model-graded benchmarks and official model cards fail to reflect true system robustness against adaptive prompt injection vectors. Consequently, reliance on benchmark evaluations masks severe security vulnerabilities in deployed AI applications.
key_points.verbatim: All models achieve near-zero ASR on standard jailbreak benchmarks per their official model cards.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Standardized benchmark evaluations fail to capture real-world vulnerabilities to adaptive prompt injection attacks.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that standardized benchmark evaluations fail to capture real-world vulnerabilities to adaptive prompt injection attacks. Encompasses: benchmark inadequacy, attack success rate disparity.

key_points.point: To evaluate the practical risks of prompt injection in agentic settings, the researchers construct a custom dataset of 100 Wikipedia pages augmented with standard and forged CoT instructions. Because existing prompt injection benchmarks do not support local models, reasoning models, and custom injections simultaneously, empirical assessment requires building specialized testing environments. This methodology underscores the difficulty of auditing complex AI systems using pre-existing evaluation frameworks.
key_points.verbatim: At the time of experimentation, we found no prompt injection benchmarks supporting local models, reasoning models, and custom injections simultaneously, necessitating a custom dataset.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Construct custom evaluation datasets to measure prompt injection vulnerabilities across diverse model architectures.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within skeptic discourse that constructs custom evaluation datasets to measure prompt injection vulnerabilities across diverse model architectures. Encompasses: custom dataset generation, multi-model evaluation.

key_points.point: The empirical findings show that commercial language models exhibit deep-seated vulnerabilities to absurd and nonsensical prompt injections, casting doubt on the reliability of current safety training and alignment paradigms. When auxiliary LLMs are instructed to generate chain-of-thought forgeries based on completely arbitrary justifications, the target models accept these absurd rationales just as readily as plausible ones. This demonstrates that models do not genuinely comprehend safety constraints but merely pattern-match against superficial linguistic styles. Skeptics point to this as evidence that current frontier models remain fundamentally unpredictable and susceptible to basic manipulation.
key_points.verbatim: The results, shown in Figure 16, provide stark evidence. The absurd justifications are surprisingly effective, achieving consistently high ASRs across all models. Crucially, the absurd policies are on average as effective—and in some cases, slightly more so—than more credible, prompt-specific justifications.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Language models easily accept absurd and nonsensical policy justifications during prompt injection, proving their safety reasoning lacks genuine comprehension.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that language models easily accept absurd and nonsensical policy justifications during prompt injection, proving their safety reasoning lacks genuine comprehension. Encompasses: absurd policy bypass, superficial pattern matching, and reasoning fragility.

key_points.point: The document investigates how long-context interactions and complex conversational flows suffer from instruction decay and position-dependent failures where early tokens dominate latent representations. The analysis of system prompts demonstrates that positional encoding acts as a dominant signal that overrides explicit container tags, causing models to forget or ignore structural hierarchy as context length increases. Untagged text or early-positioned instructions consistently outweigh later system prompts, validating concerns about the fragility of long-context model coherence. These architectural flaws mean that complex multi-turn or tool-integrated interactions are inherently susceptible to drift and hijacking.
key_points.verbatim: Untagged text in early positions approaches 100% Systemness and decays almost monotonically. The system-tagged region (purple) shows similar Systemness to the untagged tokens preceding it.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Long-context and multi-turn AI interactions suffer from instruction decay where positional bias overrides explicit structural tags.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that long-context and multi-turn AI interactions suffer from instruction decay where positional bias overrides explicit structural tags. Encompasses: positional authority dominance, system prompt failure, monotonic decay of instruction hierarchy.

key_points.point: The methodological framework relies on multi-layer activation probing across transformer layers to classify model behavior, utilizing residual stream hidden states as joint inputs for assessing role perception. By probing hidden states across model depth, the researchers show that latent representations systematically diverge from declared architectural tags. This technique provides a robust mechanism for exposing systemic discrepancies between what an AI model's interface claims and how its internal layers actually process information. Such probing methods are critical for unmasking the unreliability of model safety wrappers and structural containers.
key_points.verbatim: We evaluate each conversation, evaluating the model's internal representation under three conditions: Baseline, NoTags, and Injection. We collect hidden states for each token and aggregate by role.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Multi-layer activation probing effectively classifies internal model behavior and reveals divergences between architectural tags and latent representations.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that multi-layer activation probing effectively classifies internal model behavior and reveals divergences between architectural tags and latent representations. Encompasses: residual stream probing, latent state classification, layer-wise role tracking.

factual_claims.claim: Frontier models such as gpt-oss-20b, gpt-oss-120b, and o4-mini achieve attack success rates exceeding 80% against STRONGREJECT when subjected to CoT Forgery, despite near-zero attack success rates on raw harmful prompts and standard jailbreaks.

category_criteria.measurement_basis: StrongREJECT benchmark evaluation across six frontier models
category_criteria.falsifiability: Verifiable through replication of the CoT Forgery test suite

factual_claims.claim: In agent exfiltration tests involving 1,000 trials, attack success rises near-monotonically with probe-measured role confusion, increasing from 2% in the lowest quantile to 70% in the highest quantile.
factual_claims.claim_label: Role Confusion Predicts Agent Hijacking Success

category_criteria.measurement_basis: 1,000 agent exfiltration attempts paired with internal role probe measurements
category_criteria.falsifiability: Falsifiable by finding high attack success with low probe-measured role confusion

factual_claims.claim: Removing stylistic markers from forged chain-of-thought prompt injections collapses the attack success rate from 61% down to 10% across evaluated models.
Standard prompt injections fail with attack success rates between 0% and 2% on most models, whereas CoT forgery raises success rates to 56% through 70%.
factual_claims.claim_label: CoT Forgery Dramatically Increases Attack Success

factual_claims.claim: For CoT forgery attacks, forged reasoning achieves 79% CoTness on average, exceeding the model's genuine reasoning score of 68%, while destyling collapses this metric to 29% and causes attack failure.
factual_claims.claim_label: CoT Forgery Metrics and Destyling Impact

factual_claims.claim: In agent prompt injection experiments across 1,000 templates, attack success rates rise near-monotonically with Userness, ranging from 2% in the lowest quantile to 70% in the highest quantile.
The authors evaluated linear classifier probes across four distinct language models in the 20 billion to 120 billion parameter size range to analyze internal role representations.
factual_claims.claim_label: Model Scale and Probe Evaluation Scope

evidence_criteria.category_criteria: empirical observation of model size and probing methodology across multiple architectures

factual_claims.claim: The gpt-oss family and o4-mini models are trained using Deliberative Alignment, a process that requires models to explicitly reason about safety policies in their chain-of-thought before responding, while the GPT-5 series incorporates rule-based reasoning verification.

Auxiliary LLMs such as Gemini-2.5-Pro can be few-shot prompted with target model style references to generate forged chains-of-thought that successfully bypass safety guardrails when concatenated with harmful queries.

category_criteria.empirical_basis: Empirical attack success rate measurements across model families

factual_claims.claim: Two specific models, gpt-oss-20b and gpt-5-nano, exhibit infinite reasoning loops on certain queries, which can be stabilized by prepending a benign distractor without meaningfully impacting the attack success rate.
factual_claims.claim_label: Infinite Reasoning Loops in Small Models

category_criteria.empirical_basis: Experimental implementation notes during attack execution

factual_claims.claim: Across cross-family validation tests on frontier models including GLM-4.6, Kimi-K2-Instruct, and Minimax-M2, the chain-of-thought forgery attack transferred without modification, achieving attack success rates between 74% and 92%.

category_criteria.observational_basis: Empirical evaluation across multiple frontier model architectures using standardized test suites.
category_criteria.measurement_precision: Exact percentage success rates reported for each model family.
category_criteria.falsifiability: Can be tested by running identical injection payloads against future model versions with updated safety guardrails.

factual_claims.claim: Destyling chain-of-thought forgeries by removing characteristic lexical and syntactic markers causes attack success rates to collapse across all tested model architectures, resulting in an average drop of 51 percentage points.
factual_claims.claim_label: Impact of Destyling on Attack Success

category_criteria.observational_basis: Comparative empirical trials measuring attack success rates on standard versus destyled prompt injection variants.
category_criteria.measurement_precision: Quantified aggregate performance drop across diverse model checkpoints.
category_criteria.falsifiability: Falsifiable through independent replication of stylistic ablation experiments on alternative architectures.

factual_claims.claim: Evaluating four open-weight models under role-injection conditions reveals that stylistic cues override architectural role tags in latent space, causing userness to remain above 75% and toolness below 20% when user-style text is injected into tool data.
factual_claims.claim_label: Stylistic Cues Override Architectural Role Tags

factual_claims.claim: In 100 tool-injection agent attacks, malicious exfiltration commands embedded in tool outputs achieve 51.1% userness while forged reasoning achieves 84.1% cotness, demonstrating systematic cross-channel privilege escalation.
factual_claims.claim_label: Cross-Channel Privilege Escalation via Tool Injection

factual_claims.claim: A logistic regression model predicting instruction hierarchy failure from the systemness-to-userness ratio achieves an AUC of 0.74, substantially outperforming token count, mean activation norms, and shuffled-label controls.
factual_claims.claim_label: Role Probes Predict Instruction Hierarchy Failures
